title: Request Fragment Assembler: robust OpenAI Chat -> Redwood mapping with streaming & function-call continuity
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Context: Redwood must accept requests shaped like OpenAI Chat Completions and map them into our internal request model, and also map streamed deltas, tool/function call events, and final structured outputs back into an OpenAI-compatible streaming response. This ticket implements a robust Request Fragment Assembler that guarantees correctness in pathological streaming scenarios (partial JSON function arguments split across chunks, interleaved role changes, out-of-order deltas from upstream, and backpressure-induced buffering).

Goals:
- Ensure OpenAI-style clients (both simple and streaming consumers) see consistent semantics: deltas for content, a single function_call event with complete arguments, explicit finish_reason mapping, and proper error propagation.
- Avoid duplicating tokens or producing incomplete tool invocation payloads when streaming frames contain fragmented data.
- Maintain low latency for typical cases while protecting memory for worst-case fragmentation.

Scope and constraints:
- Implement server-side assembler that consumes Redwood-internal stream events and emits OpenAI-compatible SSE/HTTP-chunk frames.
- Handle function_call assembly: collect partial name/arguments across multiple deltas, validate against declared function signatures (where available), and only emit the final function_call payload once assembled or on a safe timeout/abort.
- Preserve role normalization: map Redwood role labels to 'system/user/assistant' and ensure legacy clients receive expected role transitions.
- Support both 'delta only' streams (tokens as they arrive) and 'full message' fallbacks for non-stream consumers.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not add new public SDK shims; it focuses on the service-side assembler and compatibility behavior. SDK changes will be handled in a follow-up.

Key design decisions (summary):
- Streaming buffer model: per-request ring buffer with configurable max bytes (default 64KB) for assembler state; when exceeded, emit a 'truncated' warning and fall back to full-message mapping for the remainder to avoid unbounded memory.
- Function-call assembly: treat 'function_call' tokens as stateful sub-streams. Maintain partial-json builder that accepts tokens until JSON is balanced or until a max-frames/time cap triggers a safe abort. On abort, emit an error frame with reason 'incomplete_function_payload' and mark request as errored for downstream metrics.
- Idempotency: preserve incoming client-provided request_id/x-request-id and propagate as X-Redwood-Compat-ID in mapped responses to enable client dedupe.

Acceptance criteria (see field below for checklist): assemble fragmented function arguments correctly in 95% of fuzzed stream scenarios; pass integration tests against an OpenAI compatibility harness; no memory growth > 2x baseline for heavy fragmentation workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Assembler produces identical final function_call payloads compared to non-streamed baseline for 1000 randomized test cases
Streaming output maps finish_reason semantics: 'stop'|'length'|'function_call' preserved and surfaced to OpenAI consumers
Partial JSON fragments concatenated and validated; invalid JSON results in a single error frame and telemetry capture
Per-request assembler memory bounded by configured ring buffer; stress tests show no unbounded growth
Behavior documented in compatibility spec and added to README; SDK teams have integration test vectors
End-to-end integration test added that verifies tool invocation only after function_call assembly completes
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-level assembler state machine (balanced braces, escape sequences, unicode splits)
Fuzz tests that simulate chunk boundaries inside ASCII/non-ASCII codepoints and JSON tokens
Integration test against OpenAI-compat harness that validates SSE framing and finish_reason mapping
Load test with synthetic fragmentation (1000 RPS) to validate memory and latency SLAs
Manual verification with cURL and node-fetch streaming clients for common and pathological cases
Postmortem scenario tests: simulate upstream truncated stream and verify proper error frames and metric increments
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'openai-compat-v2' flag for first 10% of traffic
Monitor assembler errors, function_call assembly latency, and OOM signals for 48h after each ramp step
Ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days if no regressions; automatic rollback on >3x baseline error rate
Post-rollout: add long-tail fragmented stream telemetry to Console dashboards and alerting
metrics: avg_stream_latency_ms for first token (target < 120ms for hosted-tier)
comments: 2026-02-21 - Avery Chen: Initial ticket created after spike with partner engineering; recorded examples where tool args were split across 5+ frames.
2026-02-25 - Diego Martinez: Prototype assembler implemented: supports brace balancing and simple function_call assembly. Found edge case where escaped quotes split - added unit test.
2026-03-01 - Samira Patel (PM): Reviewed prototype; requested explicit finish_reason mapping and telemetry events for partial-assembly aborts.
2026-03-05 - Diego Martinez: Added ring buffer and abort-on-overflow behavior. Integration harness failing on SSE boundary framing; investigating chunk vs event mapping.
2026-03-10 - QA (Jon Park): Added fuzz cases to CI. Two intermittent failures reproduced when non-UTF8 bytes are present; added sanitizer to drop invalid bytes and emit diagnostic metadata.
2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez: Submitted PR #6342 for assembler core; running canary behind feature flag at 5% traffic now. PR link in attachments.
notes: Trade-off: buffering more bytes reduces false-positive assembly aborts but increases memory usage. Chosen default favors safety with graceful degrade to non-streamed path.
We intentionally do not attempt to re-tokenize or re-emit exact original token boundaries; goal is semantic parity and not byte-for-byte match for deltas.
Follow-ups: SDK-level helpers to surface function_call streaming events to client apps and deterministic replay tooling for debugging assembled payloads.
Security: assembled function arguments are subject to existing KMS/PII redaction pipeline; we must ensure assembler does not leak partial PII in logs.
